faq.a: Kaveh is associated with the Persian form كَاوِه, whose core sense is kaveh; a persian legendary hero.

faq.q: What is the origin of Kaveh?
faq.a: Kaveh is associated with Persian. Kaveh is Persian کاوه (Kāveh), the name of a legendary hero in the Shahnameh. It is used as a male given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Kaveh can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Kaveh should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Kāveh is a Persian name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Kaveh mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Kaveh is rendered کاوہ and carries the sense کاوہ، فارسی ہیرو.

faq.q: What does Kaveh mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Kaveh is rendered کاوه and carries the sense کاوه، پهلوان ایرانی.
A romanized syllable approximation is ka-veh. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Kaveh?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Kaveh, kaveh. Script forms are كَاوِه, کاوه, کاوہ, कावे.

faq.q: Is Kaveh a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
